Restructuring, settlement, write-off and closure

After this lesson you can:
  • Distinguish the four endings of a distressed loan and their triggers
  • Explain restructuring's classification consequences
  • Describe OTS governance and what 'technical write-off' really means

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Restructuring: changing the deal to save it
  2. Settlement: agreeing to less
  3. Write-off: cleaning the book, keeping the claim
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS

1. Restructuring: changing the deal to save it

For a borrower in genuine difficulty with genuine intent, restructuring modifies sanctioned terms — extended tenor, revised schedule, moratorium — after a documented hardship assessment. Approval is four-eyes, re-amortisation is versioned, and the borrower is communicated.

The honesty mechanism: restructuring has classification consequences.

Restructured accounts are typically downgraded (or held in a lower classification with elevated provisioning) and must demonstrate sustained performance before upgrading.

Rules differ by framework and era — the invariant a BA can rely on: restructuring is never a free reset of the delinquency clock, because hiding stress by rescheduling was the exact abuse the rules target.

Bureau reporting also tags the account as restructured.

2. Settlement: agreeing to less

A one-time settlement (OTS) accepts less than full dues to close the exposure — rational when recovery costs exceed the recoverable. Governance is everything: a policy defines eligibility and minimum recovery; the sacrifice (amount forgone) determines the approval authority (an authority matrix — bigger sacrifice, higher approver); payment is tracked to completion; only then does the shortfall waiver execute and the account close *as settled*.

'Settled' is not 'closed normally': the bureau record says so, and it constrains the borrower's future credit. A borrower agreeing to OTS should hear that clearly — conduct includes honesty about consequences.

3. Write-off: cleaning the book, keeping the claim

A technical write-off removes the exposure from the earning book (fully provided, charged off) while retaining the legal right to recover. It is an accounting act, not debt forgiveness — recovery efforts and legal cases continue, and post-write-off recoveries credit back per policy.

Every distressed path ends at the same gate as a healthy loan: closure done right — dues resolved (paid, settled or written off), NOC where due, mandates cancelled, security released and CERSAI satisfied for secured loans, and the CIC updated with the truthful final status. The final status *is* the borrower's financial epitaph for that loan; getting it wrong is a grievance and a correction-clock violation.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-CIR-2025 — Restructured/settled/written-off statuses reach the CICs accurately; correction clocks protect the borrower.
  • RBI-DL-2025 — Conduct duties — including honest communication of consequences — persist through resolution.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Why does restructuring carry a classification consequence?

  1. To punish borrowers
  2. To prevent rescheduling from being used to hide portfolio stress
  3. Accounting convenience
  4. It doesn't
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Evergreening — rolling stress forward via reschedules — was the historic abuse; classification consequences make restructuring visible and costly enough to be honest.

2. After a technical write-off, the borrower's debt is…

  1. Forgiven entirely
  2. Transferred to CERSAI
  3. Still legally recoverable — only the book treatment changed
  4. Converted to equity
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. Write-off is an accounting removal from the earning book; the legal claim and recovery efforts persist, and recoveries credit back.
